members.name: getValue
members.description: Live content serialized in the active `format` (or an explicit one).

members.name: getContent
members.description: Alias for getValue — reads live content, not the assigned `value` input.

members.name: setValue
members.description: Replace the document with `value`, parsed in `format` (defaults to the active one).

members.name: plugins
members.description:
The editor plugin set. Assign to customise — compose with `defaultPlugins()`
to keep the built-ins, and order the array to control conflict precedence
(later plugins override earlier by id). Reassigning rebuilds the engine on the
new set, preserving the live content. Reading returns the active set.

```js
import { defaultPlugins } from '@keenmate/web-editor';
el.plugins = [...defaultPlugins(), myPlugin];
```

members.name: engine
members.description: The underlying headless engine (null before the first build / after teardown).

members.name: isReady
members.description: Whether the engine has been built and `ready` has fired.

members.name: value
members.description: Initial content to load, interpreted per `format`. Reassigning replaces the document. Reading `el.value` returns this assigned value, NOT live edits — use `getValue()` for that.

members.name: format
members.description: Serialization lens for content I/O (`value`, `getValue()`, the `change` event): 'markdown' (default), 'html', or 'json'. Switching it re-reports the SAME document in the new format — it never rebuilds the document.

members.name: mode
members.description: Presentation: 'edit' (default), 'split' (editor + live output), 'preview' (read-only render), or 'inline' (overlay chrome on a live-page element). `preview` forces read-only. Full layouts arrive in Phase 3; for now the mode is stored, reflected, and announced via `mode-change`.

members.name: isReadonly
members.description: Make the editor read-only (no input). `mode="preview"` also forces this on.

members.name: toolbar
members.description: Static toolbar edge: 'top' (default), 'bottom', 'start', or 'end' places the command toolbar flush against that side of the editor; 'none' hides it. The selection toolbar and context menu are always available while editing (independent of this).

members.name: statusbar
members.description: Status bar edge: 'none' (default), 'top', 'bottom', or 'both'. A dedicated strip of live indicators (word/char count, plus any plugin status items), hugging the editor body — separate from the toolbar zones and shown in read-only too. With 'both', items split across the two strips by their `bar` ('top'/'bottom', default 'bottom').

members.name: theme
members.description: Theme name, reflected to the host attribute for CSS theming (`:host([theme="…"])`).

members.name: anchor
members.description: For `mode="inline"` only: a CSS selector for the live-page element the floating editor card anchors to (tracked via the core positioning primitive). Absent → the inline card renders in normal flow.

members.description: Persistent slot for the static (zone) toolbar.

members.name: statusTopMount
members.description: Persistent slots for the dedicated status bar(s) — top and bottom edges.

members.name: overlayLayer
members.description: Persistent shadow-local layer the floating presenters portal into.

members.name: setDefaultOutputFormat
members.description: Seed the split output lens (before the user clicks a tab).

members.name: render
members.description:
(Re)build the shadow structure for `mode` + `toolbarSide`. The toolbar slot
and the editor mount are wrapped in one bordered `.km-surface` frame (so the
toolbar sits flush against the editor, with a divider, rather than floating as
a separate card); `toolbarSide` sets which edge the toolbar occupies. Builds
the output panel only for `split`; (re)anchors only for `inline`.

members.name: refreshOutput
members.description: Refresh the split output panel in place (no structural change).

members.name: deactivate
members.description:
Release live positioning resources without tearing down the structure.
The element calls this on `disconnect()` so a detached-but-held `inline`
editor doesn't keep a floating-ui `autoUpdate` loop running against its
detached host; a reconnect re-anchors via `render()`.

declarations.name: domRect
declarations.description:
A plain `DOMRect`-shaped object for a `@floating-ui/dom` virtual reference.
Built by hand (rather than `new DOMRect`) so it works identically in the
browser and in happy-dom, and so a caller can recompute it per frame (the
selection rect / cursor point the floating presenters anchor to).

declarations.name: wrapCommandAsPipeline
declarations.description:
Wrap a command as a trivial single-stage sync pipeline. The stage runs the PM
command via the engine-provided `runCommand`; a `false` return (command not
applicable) halts, so a keymap binding falls through correctly.

declarations.name: assemblePipelines
declarations.description:
Assemble the named pipeline map for an ordered plugin set and the engine's
assembled command specs.

declarations.name: defaultInteractionHost
declarations.description:
A sensible headless default: route an interactive request through
`window.confirm` (resolve on OK, cancel otherwise). A host that needs a richer
picker injects its own via `engine.setInteractionHost`.

members.name: on
members.description: Subscribe to a pipeline's run events. Returns an unsubscribe fn.

members.name: #services
members.description: The doc write port handed to every stage of an engine-run pipeline.

members.name: run
dispose
members.description: Abort every in-flight run (engine teardown).

declarations.name: runStagesSync
declarations.description:
Run a `sync` pipeline to completion synchronously — for triggers that ride the
browser's native synchronous events (paste / copy / keydown) and cannot await.
Stages must return an outcome directly; an async or interactive stage throws
(the design-doc contract that dialogs/awaits belong only to deferred pipelines).

declarations.name: runStages

type.text: { signal: AbortSignal; ui: InteractionHost; generation: number }

declarations.description:
Run every stage in order, threading the context. The optional `report` observer
sees each stage transition (running → ok/skipped/halted/error/aborted) for
step-level visualization. Throws only on an unexpected stage error (after
reporting it).

Debounced, cancellable runner for a single deferred pipeline. Call `schedule()`
on each change; it coalesces, runs once idle, drops stale results, and only
surfaces `pending` if the run outlasts the threshold.
declarations.name: DeferredRunner

members.name: schedule
members.description: Debounce a run. Later calls within the window reset the timer.

declarations.description: Serialize a single node to HTML (used by the table Markdown fallback).

declarations.name: coreMarkdownNodes
declarations.default: { text(state, node) { state.text(node.text || ''); }, paragraph(state, node) { state.renderInline(node); state.closeBlock(node); }, heading(state, node) { state.write(state.repeat('#', node.attrs.level) + ' '); state.renderInline(node); state.closeBlock(node); }, code_block(state, node) { state.write('```' + (node.attrs.language || '') + '\n'); state.text(node.textContent, false); state.ensureNewLine(); state.write('```'); state.closeBlock(node); }, bullet_list(state, node) { state.renderList(node, ' ', () => '- '); }, ordered_list(state, node) { const start = node.attrs.order || 1; state.renderList(node, ' ', (i: number) => `${start + i}. `); }, list_item(state, node) { state.renderContent(node); }, hard_break(state, node, parent, index) { for (let i = index + 1; i < parent.childCount; i++) { if (parent.child(i).type !== node.type) { state.write('\\\n'); return; } } }, }
declarations.description: Core node serializers (paragraph, heading, lists, code block, text, break).

declarations.name: coreMarkdownMarks
declarations.default: { bold: { open: '**', close: '**', mixable: true, expelEnclosingWhitespace: true }, italic: { open: '*', close: '*', mixable: true, expelEnclosingWhitespace: true }, underline: { open: '<u>', close: '</u>', mixable: true }, code: { open: '`', close: '`', escape: false }, }
declarations.description: Core mark serializers (bold, italic, underline, inline code).

declarations.name: coreMarkdownParse
declarations.default: { paragraph: { block: 'paragraph' }, heading: { block: 'heading', getAttrs: (tok: any) => ({ level: +tok.tag.slice(1) }) }, bullet_list: { block: 'bullet_list' }, ordered_list: { block: 'ordered_list', getAttrs: (tok: any) => ({ order: +(tok.attrGet('start') || 1) }), }, list_item: { block: 'list_item' }, fence: { block: 'code_block', getAttrs: (tok: any) => ({ language: tok.info ? tok.info.trim().split(/\s+/)[0] : 'javascript' }), }, code_block: { block: 'code_block', getAttrs: () => ({ language: 'javascript' }) }, hardbreak: { node: 'hard_break' }, em: { mark: 'italic' }, strong: { mark: 'bold' }, code_inline: { mark: 'code' }, }
declarations.description: Core token→node/mark parse specs.

declarations.name: buildMarkdownSerializer
declarations.description: Build a MarkdownSerializer from merged node/mark maps.

declarations.name: buildMarkdownParser
declarations.description:
Build a MarkdownParser for `schema` from merged parse specs. Starts from the
CommonMark preset with `blockquote` / `hr` disabled (the core schema has no
such nodes); `enableRules` re-enables markdown-it rules a plugin needs.
